explanation.explanation: Panel A is an anatomical diagram and a classification table (subtype, biomarkers, frequency), not a quantitative axis-based plot.
Panel B is a conceptual/schematic diagram (icons and text boxes) with no plotted axes.
Panel C is a schematic illustration of the experimental setup (reporter cell, luciferase gene, imaging camera) with no plotted axes.

unit_definition_as_provided.definition: Axis labeled "Days" with tick marks at 0 and 5, giving the time unit directly on the axis.

explanation.explanation: The y-axis for the three schematic luciferase traces has no numeric scale; it is used only to depict the qualitative shape of the oscillation (rhythmic, damped, arrhythmic) that later underlies the functional/unstable/weak/dysfunctional classification, not an absolute measured quantity, so no unit is required.
The x- and y-axes list categorical identifiers (numbered circadian parameters 1–7) rather than continuous quantities, so no unit applies.
The color scale (−1 to 1) represents a Pearson/Spearman-type correlation coefficient, which is inherently dimensionless.

unit_definition_as_provided.definition: Axis labeled "Days" with tick marks at 1 and 4.

explanation.explanation: The y-axis is labeled "Cell number" on a log scale (1 to 10); a cell count is a dimensionless number and needs no additional unit.

unit_definition_as_provided.definition: Axis labeled "Dose (µM)", giving the concentration unit directly on the axis.

explanation.explanation: The y-axis "Growth inh." ranges from 0 to 1, representing a dimensionless fraction/ratio of growth inhibition, which needs no unit.
Both heatmaps (gene expression and mutation) have categorical axes ("Cell line" and "Clock genes" identifiers), which require no units.

The gene-expression color scale is labeled qualitatively as "low" to "high" (relative intensity, not an absolute measurement), and the mutation heatmap uses a binary 0/1 categorical indicator; neither requires a physical unit.
The PCA plot axes (PC1, PC2) are dimensionless principal-component scores, which by convention do not carry physical units.

The 3D scatter axes ("Parameter #1/#2/#3") represent composite/derived circadian metrics obtained by integrating multiple measured parameters; as abstract composite scores analogous to principal components, they do not require conventional physical units.
